options: Production Verification Process
Productionizable Viable Product
Preliminary Validation Prototype
Parallel Virtual Platform
Provisioned Variable Pipeline
questions.explanation: PVP stands for Productionizable Viable Product.

questions.stem: What is the PVP approach designed to achieve?
options: Increase the number of environments used in a project
Replace User Acceptance Testing with automated tests
Eliminate the need for data governance
Move all analytics workloads to on-premises hardware
Reduce Time to Market for adopting cutting-edge Data and Analytics technologies while minimising CAPEX
questions.explanation: PVP is described as an approach to reduce Time to Market (TTM) for adopting cutting-edge Data and Analytics technologies while minimising Capital Expenditure.

questions.stem: On what does the PVP approach focus solely?
options: New data and analytics initiatives rather than enhancements
Enhancements to existing data solutions
Migrating legacy systems to the cloud
Security patching of production systems
Retiring old data warehouses
questions.explanation: PVP focuses solely on new data and analytics initiatives rather than enhancements.

questions.stem: What is the distinctive feature of how the PVP approach executes an IT project?
options: It uses separate development, testing and production environments from day one
It uses no environments until the final release
It employs a single Production environment throughout the project lifecycle
It builds the solution entirely in a testing environment
It outsources the production environment to a third party
questions.explanation: PVP optimises project execution by employing a singular Production environment throughout the project lifecycle, avoiding the complexity of managing multiple environments.

questions.stem: How does the PVP architecture address data privacy concerns during early development and testing?
options: By using only synthetic data generated by AI
By restricting access to the CTO alone
By deleting all personal data before the project starts
By integrating controlled measures such as data masking or anonymisation
By running the project in an isolated development environment
questions.explanation: To address privacy, PVP integrates controlled measures such as data masking or anonymisation during the initial development and testing phases, ensuring regulatory adherence.

questions.stem: How does the incremental provisioning strategy in the PVP approach begin?
options: By provisioning every service the project might ever need
By provisioning the minimum required services or tools in the Production environment
By provisioning a full development environment first
By provisioning a backup environment
By provisioning tools in the testing environment only
questions.explanation: Incremental provisioning commences with the provision of the minimum required services or tools in the Production environment.

questions.stem: By how much does the PVP approach aim to reduce Time to Market by implementing a new initiative only in Production?
options: 5 to 10 percent
10 to 20 percent
50 to 60 percent
80 to 90 percent
30 to 40 percent
questions.explanation: PVP aims to reduce Time to Market by 30 to 40 percent by implementing a new initiative only in Production.

questions.stem: By roughly how much does the PVP approach aim to decrease infrastructure investment?
options: Nearly two-thirds of the infrastructure cost
About one-tenth of the infrastructure cost
Half of the software licence cost only
The entire infrastructure cost
About one-quarter of the infrastructure cost
questions.explanation: The primary cost objective of PVP is to potentially decrease investment by nearly two-thirds of infrastructure cost, along with other costs for functions like DevOps, CI/CD and governance.

questions.stem: What is described as the primary benefit of the PVP approach if a project fails?
options: The project can be restarted in a testing environment at no cost
The vendor refunds the licence fees
The loss is limited to the cost of a single environment, namely Production
The data is automatically restored from backup
The team keeps the development environment for future projects
questions.explanation: The primary benefit is that, in the event of project failure, the loss is limited to the cost of a single environment, Production.

questions.stem: What happens after a PVP implementation is validated through User Testing sign-off?
options: The Production environment is decommissioned
The project remains permanently in a single environment
All governance practices are removed to save cost
Standard practices such as data governance, DevOps and CI/CD are initiated across development, testing and production, with PROD components provisioned in the other environments
The solution is handed to a third party for maintenance
questions.explanation: After sign-off, conventional practices are applied across all three environments and the full set of components from PROD is provisioned in development and testing, completing the SDLC cycle.
